title: Knowledge check: Introduction to Nuxt

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Introduction to Nuxt”?
options: Keep server and initial client output deterministic, isolate mutable state per request, and avoid browser-only globals during server rendering.
Assume window and document exist during every server render.
Share mutable module-scope user state across all requests.
Use random values in initial markup and assume hydration will always match.
questions.answer_key: Keep server and initial client output deterministic, isolate mutable state per request, and avoid browser-only globals during server rendering.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Introduction to Nuxt directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “What Nuxt adds to Vue”, which practice is most reliable?
options: Assume window and document exist during every server render.
Share mutable module-scope user state across all requests.
Use random values in initial markup and assume hydration will always match.
Keep server and initial client output deterministic, isolate mutable state per request, and avoid browser-only globals during server rendering.
questions.answer_key: Keep server and initial client output deterministic, isolate mutable state per request, and avoid browser-only globals during server rendering.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “What Nuxt adds to Vue”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Introduction to Nuxt” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.
